claims.claim: Energy Recovery's SEC-filed Q2 2026 results show revenue of $12.0 million, down 57% year over year, with six-month revenue down 40%; its 10-Q attributes much of the decline to lower megaproject shipments and records the wind-down of the CO2 retail grocery business after a fundamental outlook change.
Despite lower volume, Q2 gross margin was 74.7% versus 64.0% a year earlier, showing mix/cost resilience but not offsetting project-timing volatility in revenue.

risks.risk: Large desalination-project delivery timing creates pronounced quarter-to-quarter revenue volatility, and the CO2 business wind-down demonstrates technology-adjacency execution risk.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not establish whether the Q2 megaproject shipment decline is primarily timing-driven or reflects weaker forward demand.

claims.claim: Execution evidence is mixed: margin resilience is strong, but revenue contracted sharply and management exited a CO2 retail initiative, so forward expectations should distinguish core desalination economics from adjacent-market optionality.

risks.risk: High gross margin can coexist with weak shipment timing and does not by itself prove durable growth.

unknowns.unknown: Future megaproject delivery schedule and wastewater scale-up need additional source-addressed evidence.
